title: Prime-to-ell uniformization in standard form
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] whose affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$, and let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. There exist an integral scheme $X'$, a proper morphism $p:X'\to X$ inducing an isomorphism over a dense open of $X$, a finite family of separated etale morphisms $e_i:E_i\to X'$ of finite type, finite locally free surjective morphisms $a_i:W_i\to E_i$ of constant positive ranks $r_i$ prime to $\ell$, finitely many regular Noetherian schemes $Y_b$, and $X$-morphisms $W_i\to Y=\coprod_bY_b$. The schemes $X',E_i,W_i,Y_b$ are of finite type over $X$. The family $(e_i)$ is completely decomposed: for every $x'\in X'$ there are $i$ and $z\in E_i$ over $x'$ with $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(z)$ an isomorphism. For every $b$, the inverse image $U\times_XY_b$ is the complement of a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] in $Y_b$. Proper, finite and flat have the meanings of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism], etale that of [def-weil-etale-morphism], and regular that of [def-weil-regular-scheme].
